title: Rabbi Abba bar Zutra, or Rava bar Zutra
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Hyman writes: He was a student of R' Chanina (see Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 4:4). The statement is likewise cited in Avodah Zarah 28b, where see: Rabbah ba Zutra in the name of R' Chanina; so too in Jerusalem Talmud Avodah Zarah, chapter 2, beginning of halakha 2, and in Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 4:11. It seems that he went to Babylonia for a short time, and therefore we find that he said in the name of Shmuel (Yevamot 4:11) the wonderful statement, "Whatever has a heh, rava [רבא]; and with an alef, rava [רבא]." Some explain that this refers to the names of amoraim, that if written with a heh it is Rabbah and with an alef it is Rava, but they are mistaken, for what connection does Shmuel's statement have to Rabbah and Rava? Rather, the true reading is as cited in Jerusalem Talmud Niddah 1:3: "Whatever is in 'harbeh' is in 'arbeh'" — meaning, whoever is born at 212 days, the numerical value of "harbeh," which is seven complete months, will live and multiply. So I found in the commentary of Maharzu on Bereshit Rabbah, at the supplied locator פ״ק-ו. So too we find that he said in the name of Shmuel in Midrash Shmuel, beginning of chapter 15. While in Babylonia he learned the Aramaic language.

Hyman continues: Afterwards he returned to the Land of Israel and became the interpreter (meturgeman) of Rabbi Yochanan, to release a woman from her vow, because she did not understand the language called sotiston in the supplied entry [the named Ran reads Suriston] (Jerusalem Talmud Nedarim 10:8, and cited in the Ran at 8b).

Hyman further reports: He is mentioned in Bava Metzia 16a and Bava Batra 24b, according to the reading of D-K-S, where he answered: "This requires no further explanation." Those who say [teachings] in his name that we find include only R' Zeira (Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 14:4, Yevamot 4:11, and Avodah Zarah, chapter 2, beginning of halakha 2).

notes.text: Hyman rejects interpreting the heh/alef saying as the amora names Rabbah/Rava and instead invokes harbeh/arbeh,212days and seven complete months. The supplied Bereshit Rabbah locator פ״ק-ו remains unresolved.

The exact language designation sotiston and the Nedarim/Ran passage still need checking. In Hyman’s account the interpreter serves Rabbi Yochanan; Abba/Rava/Rabbah bar Zutra are the supplied name forms.

The whole saved Vilna Ran on Nedarim8b identifies the woman as the person who did not understand Suriston. The earlier English assigning that difficulty to Rabbi Yochanan remains archived. The supplied sotiston (סוטיסטון) is retained beside the Ran's Suriston (סוריסטון), without changing the Hebrew. The Ran locally supplies full Rabbi Abba bar Zutra and Rabbi Yochanan; the other abbreviated personal titles remain R'. The heading's Abba/Rava bar Zutra and the body's Rabbah ba Zutra remain distinct supplied forms. The initial heh/alef quotation actually has רבא in both places; both are retained as rava with Hebrew brackets, while Hyman's following Rabbah/Rava explanation and his emphatic rejection remain unchanged. His true-reading claim,212days,seven complete months,travel and language-learning narrative remain attributed to him, without a new medical or historical admission. The Maharzu locator פ״ק-ו, the supplied Yerushalmi numbering and both source holds remain. D-K-S retains the supplied abbreviation; its earlier probable Dikdukei Soferim expansion remains archived without a fresh collation. Only Zeira is Hyman's stated finding, rather than a fresh whole-corpus absence claim. All earlier English and mixed notes remain preserved; no printing-history claim or extra Ran legal material is imported.

The printed notice in Hyman I, p.45, has Rabbah in the alternative heading, beside Rava in the supplied Wikisource heading; the supplied Hebrew and title are retained. Its language name is Suriston, as in the whole consulted Ran on Nedarim 8b, while the supplied text has sotiston and the consulted Guggenheimer Yerushalmi Nedarim 10:8 has סוריבטין. In both the Ran and Yerushalmi, the woman is the person who did not understand the language. The whole Avodah Zarah 28b paragraph has Rabbah bar Zutra reporting Rabbi Chanina, beside Hyman’s Rabbah ba Zutra; these forms are not globally merged. The whole Yerushalmi Yevamot 4:11 passage prints the heh/alef saying in braces and harbeh/arbeh in brackets; its English commentary gives 208 days. The parallel Niddah 1:3 Hebrew instead has בארבע and its English gives 273. These consulted readings are compared with Hyman’s retained, emphatic argument for harbeh/arbeh and 212 days, seven complete months; his number and conclusion have not been silently normalized. The quoted report in the whole Krakow 1893 Midrash Shmuel 15 opening names Rabbi Shmuel, which does not independently identify him with the Babylonian Shmuel or establish Hyman’s travel and language-learning reconstruction. The supplied Maharzu locator פ״ק-ו remains uncollated. The exact D-K-S readings at Bava Metzia 16a and Bava Batra 24b remain Hyman’s report, and “only Zeira” remains his stated finding rather than a new corpus-wide absence claim.
